title: Dhamaal 4 Has Crossed ₹100 Crore Worldwide. Nobody's Laughing at the Franchise Anymore.
excerpt: From a ₹7 crore opening in 2007 to a ₹100 crore global smash in five days — Indra Kumar's comedy sequel just rewrote the rules for Bollywood's most underestimated genre
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Dhamaal 4 crossed ₹100 crore worldwide in just five days.
  • The film's opening weekend grossed ₹64.35 crore, the highest in the franchise.
  • Sunday's collection reached ₹28.15 crore, the third-highest for post-pandemic comedies.
  • Overseas earnings stand at approximately $1.6 million, led by North America.
  • Bollywood comedies have struggled recently, but Dhamaal 4 is thriving.
Franchise Growth Over Time

There was a time — not very long ago — when Bollywood's comedy sequels were considered safe bets at best and diminishing returns at worst. Nobody was building franchises around them. Nobody was tracking their overseas numbers. And absolutely nobody was expecting a film about four idiots chasing pirate treasure to cross ₹100 crore worldwide in under a week. https://youtube.com/watch?v=IG-eByZdz6Y **Dhamaal 4** just did exactly that. Director **Indra Kumar's** fourth installment in the franchise crossed the ₹100 crore worldwide gross milestone on its fourth day, Monday, and by Tuesday had pushed past ₹102 crore. In India alone, the film has collected ₹73.33 crore net (approximately ₹87 crore gross), with overseas markets contributing an additional ₹15.28 crore. The worldwide gross now stands at ₹102.58 crore — a figure that puts it comfortably ahead of where *Total Dhamaal* stood at the same stage seven years ago. But the real story isn't the number. It's the trajectory. ## A Franchise That Kept Getting Bigger Consider where this franchise started. The original *Dhamaal* opened in 2007 with a first weekend of just ₹7.08 crore. It was a scrappy little comedy with no big-ticket star power, built entirely on the chaotic energy of **Arshad Warsi**, **Riteish Deshmukh**, **Javed Jaffrey**, and a pre-superstardom Sanjay Dutt. It found its audience slowly, the way comedies used to. *Double Dhamaal* in 2011 tripled that to ₹21.75 crore. *Total Dhamaal* in 2019, buoyed by the addition of **Ajay Devgn** and a much larger marketing push, jumped to ₹62.40 crore. And now *Dhamaal 4*, with the same core trio plus new additions **Ravi Kishan**, **Sanjeeda Shaikh**, and **Esha Gupta**, has opened at ₹64.35 crore — officially the biggest opening weekend in franchise history. That is a nine-fold increase in opening weekend collections over nineteen years. No Bollywood comedy franchise has grown like this. https://www.instagram.com/p/DamVWGno3zp/ ## The Sunday That Changed the Conversation The film's breakout day was Sunday, its third, when it collected ₹28.15 crore net — the **third-highest single-day collection for any comedy in the post-pandemic era**, trailing only the Day 2 and Day 3 figures of *Housefull 5*. It even outpaced the opening day of *Housefull 5* itself (₹24 crore) and eclipsed the best single-day performance of *Welcome To The Jungle* (₹24.75 crore). What drove it was old-fashioned theatrical energy. On BookMyShow alone, the film sold over 12.53 lakh tickets across the weekend — 4.55 lakh on Saturday and 4.35 lakh on Sunday. Walk-in crowds at multiplexes pushed the Sunday occupancy past 44 per cent. Pune led the way at 28 per cent, followed by Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, and Mumbai, all crossing 22 per cent. The Monday drop to ₹8.18 crore was steeper than *Total Dhamaal's* first Monday (₹9.85 crore), but the four-day total of ₹73.75 crore had already overtaken the predecessor's ₹72.25 crore. Tuesday's discounted-ticket surge pushed the net collection past ₹74 crore, with early booking velocity outpacing Monday.
Record-Breaking Sunday
›3rd highest for post-pandemic comedies Sunday collection: ₹28.15 crore

›4.55 lakh on Saturday, 4.35 lakh on Sunday Total tickets sold on BookMyShow: 12.53 lakh

## Why This Matters for the Diaspora Overseas, the film has earned approximately $1.6 million so far, with North America leading at $508,000 (roughly ₹4.27 crore). Those numbers won't trouble *Dhurandhar's* records, but they confirm something that Bollywood's comedy genre has struggled to prove: family comedies can travel. For NRI families looking for a clean, kid-friendly multiplex outing — the kind of film you can take your parents and your twelve-year-old to without anyone cringing — *Dhamaal 4* is an increasingly rare commodity. The CBFC passed it with a U/A 13+ certificate and zero scene cuts. In a release slate dominated by dark spy thrillers and emotionally heavy biopics, that counts for something. ## The Bigger Picture Bollywood released over a dozen comedies in 2026 so far. Most of them flopped. *Baby Do Die Do* earned ₹4.72 crore lifetime. *Daadi Ki Shaadi* managed ₹82 lakh in its first week in the United States. The genre has been written off so many times that its survival now feels like a punchline nobody expected to land. But *Dhamaal 4* isn't surviving. It's thriving. And the reason is deceptively simple: it knew what it was. Not a social commentary wearing a comedy mask. Not a rom-com pretending to be edgy. Just four grown men doing spectacularly stupid things with enough warmth and energy to fill a theatre on a Sunday afternoon. Indra Kumar has been doing this since *Dil* in 1990. He's never won a National Award. He's never been invited to Cannes. But he might just have the best instinct for what makes an Indian family laugh of any working director in the industry.
Overseas Appeal of Dhamaal 4
›₹4.27 crore from North America Overseas earnings: $1.6 million
›No scene cuts Family-friendly content with U/A 13+ certificate
›Most comedies in 2026 flopped Contrast with darker Bollywood releases
The film is now chasing ₹125 crore worldwide by the end of its first week — a target that looked absurd before Thursday and now looks entirely achievable. Nobody saw this coming. Least of all the people who keep writing Bollywood comedy's obituary.
